summary.intent: Finish work package W: reduce git process spawning in tag history probing for foreign tags in the callisto CLI, then push the branch and open a draft PR linked to trail #462.
summary.outcome: Fix implemented and pushed to worktree-wp-w-history-cache (draft PR #576, linked to trail #462). Git processes for `status` with foreign tags fell from 64/304/1,204 to a constant 17, and mutation testing reported 0 missed mutants. `just ci` and real-registry checks were not run.

repo: Tag selection lives in `select_last_tag`, now the first element of the new `rank_tags`, which parses and orders candidates once. Version and tag-name tie-breaking and E's literal-name ownership must stay unchanged.
`just bench` has a `foreign tags` shape. `CALLISTO_BENCH_SHAPES=1` also lists the git processes spawned.
A cascade test expects only `tag --list` in workspaces, so any extra git process on the happy path breaks it. Commits must be read only after a tag is rejected.
Cargo and pnpm workspaces have fixed process counts for `status`, `version --dry-run` and `release --dry-run` (8, 16, 11), which serve as a regression baseline.
Changes need a changeset; this one is a `callisto-cli` patch in `.changeset/noble-cobras-surge.md`.
Pre-merge gates are `just pre-push`, `just lint`, `just doc-check` and `just test`. `just ci` is separate and heavier.
A `mutants.out*` directory can appear after `cargo mutants` and must not be tracked or committed.
workflow: Run `cargo mutants --in-diff` on the changed Rust to find test gaps. Here it exposed that the process-count test did not check that every tag was rejected, which led to a regression test.
Verify a push with `git ls-remote` against `git rev-parse HEAD`, and check commit signature validity through `gh api ... commit.verification.reason`.

`entire trail link <n> --base main` links the branch to a trail, and the PR body carries an Entire marker. Append the write-up below the marker and keep the marker intact when editing the body with `gh pr edit --body-file`.
A fresh-context reviewer subagent (Opus) was used for an independent review before the PR was opened.
Wall-clock benchmarks on a shared machine are noisy, so report process counts as the primary metric and wall times as single medians.

friction: The first version read commits up front, which added one git process to every workspace and broke a cascade test. It was redesigned to read commits lazily after a rejection.
The first mutation run missed two mutants on `rev_of` because the tests checked counts but not that all tags were rejected.
The PR body held only Entire's marker, so it needed manual augmentation.
open_items: `just ci` was not run on the final commit.
The PR is still a draft and awaits review and merge.
Wall-time figures are single medians from a shared machine and may need a cleaner re-measurement.
